headline: KSE-100 dips 200 points in volatile session as Moody's lifts Pakistan to B3, while Wall Street splits and oil slides on historic Iran sanctions
mood: Mixed cross-currents · sovereign upgrade offset by Fed and sanctions risk

five_things.chip: KSE-100 dips 200 points despite Moody's B3 upgrade
five_things.html: The benchmark closed Monday at 176,966.69, down 199.84 points (0.11%) after swinging from an intraday high of 178,122.88 to a low of 176,735.57 on profit-taking in ENGROH, MEBL, SRVI, SYS and MCB (−453 points combined), even as OGDC, PPL, MLCF, DGKC and FCCL added 392 points; volume held firm at 930m shares worth Rs44bn, led by CNERGY (266m shares). Breadth stayed slightly negative (222 advancers vs 241 decliners of 498 traded). The session came hours after Moody's upgraded Pakistan's sovereign rating to B3 from Caa1 (stable outlook), citing FX reserves near $17bn (from $14bn a year earlier) and interest payments falling to ~35% of revenue from 49%. Sources: Express Tribune, Business Recorder.

five_things.chip: Wall Street splits as chip stocks slide, Fed awaits Jackson Hole
five_things.html: The Dow added 140.15 points (0.3%) to 53,417.16, while the S&P 500 slipped 0.3% to 7,652.86 and the Nasdaq fell 0.8% to 25,980.19 as chip stocks sank — Micron dropped 5.8%, AMD and Broadcom lost more than 3% and 2% respectively — even as Treasury yields eased, with the 10-year near 4.72% and the 2-year near 4.19%. The FOMC held its rate at 3.50%-3.75% on 29 July (9-3, three dissents favouring a hike), and markets now await Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's first Jackson Hole address on Friday, 28 August, just weeks ahead of the 16 September decision. Sources: Washington Post, Tech Times.

five_things.chip: Gold nears $4,660, silver holds near $69 on Fed and PCE positioning
five_things.html: Spot gold traded near $4,652–4,657/oz (+~1.2%), just off the $4,660 mark, while silver held near $69/oz (+0.4%), with haven demand framed by this week's PCE inflation print and Chair Warsh's looming Jackson Hole remarks. Sources: Kitco, Yahoo Finance.

five_things.chip: Oil slides despite ‘toughest-ever’ US sanctions on Iran
five_things.html: Brent fell 2.5% to $92.06/bbl and WTI dropped 2.5% to $84.89/bbl even as the Trump administration unveiled a sweeping new sanctions regime — dubbed "Operation Economic Outcast" — that Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent called an "economic D-Day" against Iran, with China not exempted; the sell-off suggests traders see limited near-term risk to actual supply despite Iran's warning of possible Hormuz ship seizures. Sources: CNBC, CNBC.

five_things.chip: GCC: OPEC+ holds output path, Saudi PMI eases, PIF presses 2026-2030 strategy
five_things.html: Seven OPEC+ members kept to their fifth straight monthly increase of 188,000 bpd in August even as Hormuz-linked shipping risk clouds actual barrels moved; Saudi Arabia's non-oil private sector expanded at a slightly softer pace in July (Riyad Bank PMI 53.1, down from 53.3), while PIF continued rolling out its 2026-2030 strategy — published 12 August with a tilt toward tourism, entertainment and private-sector co-investment — following its completed acquisition of Electronic Arts alongside Silver Lake and Affinity Partners on 4 August. Sources: AGBI, PIF.

matrix.local_html: The KSE-100 slipped 199.84 points (0.11%) to close at 176,966.69 on Monday, swinging between an intraday high of 178,122.88 and a low of 176,735.57 as profit-taking in ENGROH, MEBL, SRVI, SYS and MCB (−453 points combined) offset gains in OGDC, PPL, MLCF, DGKC and FCCL (+392 points); volume was healthy at 930m shares worth Rs44bn, led by CNERGY (266m shares), with breadth modestly negative (222 gainers vs 241 losers of 498 traded). The session followed Moody's upgrade of Pakistan's sovereign rating to B3 from Caa1 (stable outlook) on governance gains and easing external risk — FX reserves near $17bn versus $14bn a year earlier, and interest payments down to ~35% of revenue from 49% — extending the momentum from S&P's B upgrade on 22 July. July CPI eased to 9.2% y/y from 11.1% in June, the SBP held its policy rate at 11.5% for a second straight meeting, and KIBOR sat near 11.39/11.89% as of 20 August; an IMF mission is expected in September for the next EFF/RSF review, with roughly $1.2bn in view.
matrix.gcc_html: Brent fell 2.5% to $92.06/bbl and WTI dropped to $84.89/bbl even as Washington unveiled its toughest-ever Iran sanctions package, with Tehran warning of possible Strait of Hormuz ship seizures in response. Seven OPEC+ members continued a fifth straight 188,000 bpd monthly output increase, while Saudi Arabia's non-oil private sector expanded at a slightly softer pace in July (Riyad Bank PMI 53.1, down from 53.3 in June). Separately, PIF's 2026-2030 strategy, published 12 August, deepens its tilt toward tourism, entertainment and private-sector co-investment, on the heels of its completed Electronic Arts acquisition with Silver Lake and Affinity Partners on 4 August — the diversification anchor even as Hormuz-linked shipping risk clouds the near-term oil outlook.
matrix.global_html: Wall Street was split Monday — the Dow added 0.3% to 53,417.16 while the S&P 500 slipped 0.3% to 7,652.86 and the Nasdaq fell 0.8% to 25,980.19 as chip stocks sold off (Micron −5.8%, AMD and Broadcom down more than 3% and 2%); Treasury yields eased, with the 10-year near 4.72% and the 2-year near 4.19%, ahead of Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's first Jackson Hole address on Friday, 28 August — nineteen days before the 16 September FOMC decision, where markets are pricing roughly one-in-three odds of a hike after the 9-3 hold on 29 July. Washington simultaneously rolled out its toughest-ever sanctions regime against Iran — "Operation Economic Outcast", per Treasury Secretary Bessent — while Canada vowed retaliatory tariffs after President Trump threatened a 50% levy on Canadian autos, parts and steel. Gold held firm near $4,652-4,657/oz and silver near $69/oz as havens stayed bid into the policy-heavy week.

legislative.policy_html: Moody's upgrades Pakistan to B3 from Caa1 (stable outlook) on 24 August, citing stronger governance and external buffers; SBP holds its policy rate at 11.5% for a second straight meeting as July CPI eases to 9.2%, with an IMF mission expected in September for the next EFF/RSF review (~$1.2bn in view).
legislative.sectors: Banks, Sovereign bonds, Equities, IMF-linked sovereign risk
legislative.impact_html: Wins: sovereign bondholders and banks holding government paper as the upgrade lowers external financing costs, and exporters/importers if the ~$1.2bn IMF tranche clears on schedule. Loses: leveraged borrowers and rate-sensitive sectors (autos, cement, construction) still financing at 11.5%, with Pakistan's B3 rating still seven notches below investment grade.

legislative.policy_html: Seven OPEC+ members roll over a fifth straight 188,000 bpd monthly output increase even as Iran warns of possible Hormuz ship seizures; PIF's 2026-2030 strategy, published 12 August, deepens its private-sector, tourism-led diversification push.
legislative.sectors: Energy, Oil exporters, Tourism/PIF portfolio, Shipping/Insurance
legislative.impact_html: Wins: PIF-linked tourism, entertainment and gaming assets (including the newly closed Electronic Arts deal) under the refreshed strategy, and Gulf oil exporters if the Hormuz risk premium reasserts itself. Loses: Saudi Arabia's broader non-oil momentum, which softened slightly in July (PMI 53.1 vs 53.3), and shippers/insurers exposed to the escalating Hormuz standoff.

legislative.policy_html: The US unveils its toughest-ever Iran sanctions regime — "Operation Economic Outcast" — on 24 August, extending pressure to China's trade with Tehran, while Canada vows retaliatory tariffs after Trump threatened 50% duties on Canadian autos, parts and steel.
legislative.impact_html: Wins: gold and other havens as sanctions and tariff escalation lift geopolitical risk premia, plus US sanctions-compliance and trade-advisory firms. Loses: chipmakers already under pressure (Micron, AMD, Broadcom fell Monday) and cross-border autos/steel exporters facing the threatened 50% US tariff on Canadian goods.

levels.support_note: session's key floor per desk technicals; deeper support near 173,500
levels.resistance_note: Monday's intraday high; a clean break opens 178,700

desk_stance_html: The desk reads Monday's dip as consolidation, not reversal: Moody's B3 upgrade and the improving reserves/interest-payment trajectory argue for a constructive medium-term PSX view, but near-term price action stays tethered to global cross-currents — a hawkish-leaning Fed heading into Chair Warsh's Jackson Hole address on 28 August, and a fresh US-Iran sanctions escalation that has so far left oil sellers unfazed. We'd fade weakness toward 175,000 support and take a cautious approach above 178,100 resistance pending clarity from Jackson Hole and the September IMF mission. All levels are indicative desk estimates, not recommendations.

THE OVERNIGHT TAPE
Wall Street was split Monday: the Dow added 0.3% to 53,417.16, the S&P 500 slipped 0.3% to 7,652.86 and the Nasdaq fell 0.8% to 25,980.19 as chip stocks sold off (Micron -5.8%, AMD and Broadcom down more than 3% and 2%). The 10-year Treasury eased to ~4.72% and the 2-year to ~4.19% as markets look ahead to Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's first Jackson Hole address on Friday, 28 August — nineteen days before the 16 September FOMC decision. Gold held firm near $4,652-4,657/oz and silver near $69/oz.

PAKISTAN
The KSE-100 slipped 199.84 points (0.11%) to close at 176,966.69, swinging between an intraday high of 178,122.88 and a low of 176,735.57. Profit-taking in ENGROH, MEBL, SRVI, SYS and MCB (-453 points combined) offset gains in OGDC, PPL, MLCF, DGKC and FCCL (+392 points); volume held firm at 930m shares worth Rs44bn, led by CNERGY. The session followed Moody's upgrade of Pakistan's sovereign rating to B3 from Caa1 (stable outlook), citing FX reserves near $17bn (from $14bn a year earlier) and interest payments falling to ~35% of revenue from 49%. July CPI eased to 9.2% y/y, the SBP held its rate at 11.5%, and an IMF mission is expected in September for the next EFF/RSF review (~$1.2bn in view).

GCC
Brent fell 2.5% to $92.06/bbl and WTI to $84.89/bbl even as Washington unveiled its toughest-ever Iran sanctions package, with Tehran warning of possible Hormuz ship seizures. OPEC+ continued a fifth straight 188,000 bpd monthly output increase, while Saudi Arabia's non-oil PMI eased slightly to 53.1 in July. PIF's 2026-2030 strategy, published 12 August, deepens its tourism and private-sector-led diversification push, on the heels of its completed Electronic Arts acquisition.

GLOBAL
The US rolled out "Operation Economic Outcast" against Iran — Treasury Secretary Bessent's "economic D-Day" — while Canada vowed retaliatory tariffs after President Trump threatened a 50% levy on Canadian autos, parts and steel.

LEGISLATIVE TRACKER
- Pakistan: Moody's B3 upgrade + SBP hold at 11.5% + September IMF review. Wins: bondholders, banks, exporters. Loses: leveraged borrowers still at 11.5%.
- GCC: OPEC+ output rollover + PIF 2026-2030 strategy. Wins: PIF-linked tourism/gaming, oil exporters. Loses: Saudi non-oil momentum, shippers/insurers.
- Global: US Iran sanctions + Canada tariff retaliation. Wins: gold, havens, compliance advisors. Loses: chipmakers, autos/steel exporters.

THE DAY AHEAD
KSE-100 support 175,000 (deeper support 173,500) · pivot 176,967 (Monday's close) · resistance 178,100 (Monday's intraday high, then 178,700). We'd fade weakness toward support and take a cautious approach above resistance pending clarity from Jackson Hole and the September IMF mission.
